newsitem.title: USA: Sightseeing ship slices into New York building.
newsitem.headline: Sightseeing ship slices into New York building.

text.p: In an example of life imitating the seventh art, a New York sightseeing ship crashed into a riverfront building on Friday, embedding its bow in a wall.
The ship was carrying 520 passengers, and a dozen people were injured and taken to nearby hospitals, authorities said. The most serious injury was a broken leg, they said.
The summer action picture "Speed 2: Cruise Control" climaxes with an out-of-control cruise liner running up on land and trashing a Caribbean town.
The cause of the New York crash was unknown and under investigation but may been have a mechanical problem, Coast Guard spokesman Lionel Bryant said.

The 156-foot (47.55 metre) 'Spirit of New York' hit a building at Pier 62 on the West Side of Manhattan at about 2 p.m., the Coast Guard said. The ship, which carries passengers on trips around New York harbor, normally docks at nearby Pier 61.
"It sounded like an explosion, but it continued and continued," one man who was working nearby said.

The bow of the ship lodged 11 feet (3.4 metres) into the side of the building, an equestrian center that was still under construction and not in use, the Fire Department said. The equestrian center was part of Chelsea Piers, a big recreational center at 12th Avenue and 23rd Street in Manhattan.
Coast Guard and other emergency workers were attempting to free the ship before the changing tide shifted its position, Bryant said. There was no sign of any spilled oil, he said.

Last week a young man drowned after jumping from the same ship, which had been rented for a high school senior prom, police said. The incident occurred in the early morning as the 'Spirit of New York' was docking at the South Street Seaport, a popular tourist spot in southern Manhattan.
